- Either the literal "0" 
- Or a character from [1-9A-Za-z-] followed by zero or more characters from [0-9A-Za-z-]

So "00" would try to match "0" first, leaving "0" unmatched, so it fails. Then it tries the second alternative starting with "0" but "0" is not in [1-9A-Za-z-], so that fails too. Good, so leading zeros are correctly rejected.

- Pre-release identifiers MUST comprise only ASCII alphanumerics and hyphens [0-9A-Za-z-]

The current regex uses `(?:0|[1-9A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*)` which handles the leading zero rule correctly.

```

This allows:
